Surah 103: Al-'Asr (The Declining Day)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By time (al-'asr),﴾ He swears by the prayer of 'Asr, because of its excellence, as evidenced by His saying (Exalted is He): "And the middle prayer, the prayer of 'Asr" [2:238], in the codex of Hafsah. And because the obligation to perform it is more difficult, owing to people's preoccupation with their trade and gains at the end of the day and their busyness with their livelihoods. Or He swears by the afternoon (al-'ashiyy), just as He swears by the forenoon (al-duha) [93:1], because of the signs of power in it. Or He swears by time, because in its passing are various kinds of wonders. And the answer to the oath is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 103, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾ That is: the species of mankind is in loss, in their trade (their dealings).

Al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil (Commentary on Surah 103, verse 3):

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they have bought the Hereafter with the worldly life, so they profited and were made happy.

﴿And advise one another to truth﴾, to the matter that is established and cannot be denied, and which is all good: from the Oneness of Allah, obedience to Him, and following His books and His messengers.

﴿And advise one another to patience﴾, against sins, or upon acts of obedience, and upon what Allah tests His servants with. And "tawasaw" (they advised one another), in both places, is a past-tense verb, conjoined (ma'tuf) upon the past-tense verb before it.
